prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable solution has electrified freight corridors at anything near the Main KPI of 500,000 kilometres of electrified road; what is deployed is a handful of short demonstrators. Electric road systems exist only as short demonstrators: the German ELISA overhead-line trial on the A5 is about 10 km and lost ministry funding, about ten operational demonstrators existed worldwide in 2024, Sweden cancelled its E20 permanent electric road procurement in 2023 after bids exceeded budget and paused the work in December 2024, and the UK found dynamic wireless charging 3 to 10 times the cost of conductive charging (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_road). A 2024 review argues field trials are sufficient and Europe must decide and act (https://doi.org/10.1088/2634-4505/ad3576), while 2026 work still compares corridor costs of static megawatt charging against electric roads in Germany (https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7213899), so even the choice of technology is unresolved. GitHub has no open electric-road planning or deployment code. Honest limit: catenary, conductive-rail and inductive hardware is known and demonstrated, so tasks that re-run the ELISA or Swedish pilot designs are known answers; the open, checkable work is corridor economics, grid integration and the electric-road versus battery-charging decision, while laying the road itself is infrastructure finance beyond a research task.
